title: Articles and Describing People with ser

sections.title: Articles and ser + adjective
sections.content: Spanish nouns have gender. Use 'el' or 'un' before masculine nouns, and 'la' or 'una' before feminine ones ('el/la' = the, 'un/una' = a/an). To describe someone, use 'ser' + an adjective, and make the adjective agree: adjectives ending in -o change to -a for feminine (organizado → organizada, tranquilo → tranquila); adjectives already ending in -e don't change (parecido/a does, but inteligente stays the same for both).

items.spanish: Ella es chilena y es profesora de español.
items.english: She's Chilean and she's a Spanish teacher.

items.spanish: Kaylee habla mucho y siempre hace bromas.
items.english: Kaylee talks a lot and always makes jokes.
Now I understand! They're very alike.

sections.content: 'Un intercambio' (masculine, ends in a consonant) and 'una fiesta' (feminine) show that you can't always guess gender from meaning — it's worth learning the article together with each new noun.
